name: Collins 2013 Shiva amygdaloid: CCW 100->240 ms, 4-s gaps (20 min)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Collins & Persinger 2013; Collins 2013 MA thesis), on Todd Murphy's 64-coil Shiva hat
summary: The 20-min field condition of Collins & Persinger 2013: Shiva's "amygdaloid signal, normal speed" (289 points of 3 ms, then 4 s of silence) stepped counter-clockwise around the head, 100 ms on the left frontal position and 20 ms longer on each next one. Persinger's lab reported more out-of-body, "somewhere else" and presence experiences than in a sham group (5 vs 4 people) and no rise in temporal delta power.
notes: Thesis method: a construction-worker hat from Todd Murphy with 8 columns of 8 solenoids at equal angles over the EEG cap, driven by Shiva Neural Stimulation Software 5E through four USB audio devices, each feeding two successive columns; 289 points of -5 to +5 V at 3 ms with 4000 ms between cycles; 100 ms on the left frontal column and "an additional 20 ms" on each next column counter-clockwise from the top (100 ... 240 ms, a 1.36-s turn); about 1 uT (10 mG) in the head. Here one coil stands for each column, on Murphy's Shiva ring starting at Fp1 (an inference; the column positions are not given). The amygdaloid file was never published; the built-in accelerating burst (6-30 Hz) on 289 points of 3 ms stands in, and the rotation runs continuously (how Shiva aligned burst and columns is not described). murphy-shiva-amygdala-simple-normal is Murphy's own version (230 points, 10-20 ms per coil); murphy-shiva64-obe-lab is the 5-min single case of Saroka et al. 2010. Results: 9 university volunteers aged 20-25 (5 field, 4 sham), told they might or might not get a field; field subjects endorsed 35 % vs 9 % of 20 exit-questionnaire items (t(7) = 3.11), with effect-size r of .58-.76 for presence, dizziness, terror or fear, leaving the body and being somewhere else; the sham group's temporal delta power rose over the 20 min while the field group's did not. Tiny sample, subjective endpoints, experimenter blinding not reported, never replicated; subjects sat in a dark chamber knowing a field might come, the setting in which Granqvist et al. tied such reports to suggestibility. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on fear, headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated in a comfortable chair in a quiet, dark room (originally a shielded acoustic chamber), eyes closed for the whole 20 min. The lab took 30-s EEG samples before the field and at 5, 10, 15 and 20 min, and gave a 20-item exit questionnaire afterwards.
schedule: One 20-min session in the original. For a self-test, use the app's Blind option so the helmet picks field or sham, and fill in the questionnaire before the result is revealed.
source: Collins & Persinger 2013, Changing velocity circumcerebral magnetic fields produce altered state experiences and lowered delta-theta power over the temporal lobes, Review of Psychology Frontier 2(2):26-29 ; Collins 2013, Quantitative differences in participants exposed to patterned, weak-intensity electromagnetic fields: investigating the Shiva, MA thesis (Psychology), Laurentian University, ch. 2 https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/c03e0259-4b31-410f-9552-d90c9c2b81a4/content ; Saroka, Mulligan, Murphy & Persinger 2010, NeuroQuantology 8(4):466-477 https://www.researchgate.net/publication/275606923_Experimental_Elicitation_of_an_Out_of_Body_Experience_and_Concomitant_Cross-Hemispheric_Electroencephalographic_Coherence ; Murphy, Shiva coil locations https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/shiva/shiva_demo/locations.htm ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
